title: Rank-one derived difference model for countable ind-unipotent norm-coefficient modules
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, a finite intermediate field $E$, and $F=E$ or $F=\Omega$. Put $A(S)=C(S,F)$, using all continuous maps on the coherent profinite site [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], in compatible universes containing all profinite parameter sets [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G$ be any profinite group (a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group), and put $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ with its inverse-limit topology. Use ordinary internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and condensed group actions [def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

Let $V_0\subseteq V_1\subseteq\cdots$ be a sequence of finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector spaces with injective $E$-linear transition maps. For every $n$, let $D_n:V_n\to V_n$ be nilpotent, meaning $D_n^{e_n}=0$ for some integer $e_n\geq1$. Assume the $D_n$ commute with transition maps. Give each $V_n$ a continuous $E$-linear $G$-action, compatible with transition maps and commuting with $D_n$. Give $H$ the action
$$t\cdot v=\exp(tD_n)v=\sum_{j=0}^{e_n-1}\frac{t^jD_n^jv}{j!}.$$
This is a finite sum, with $t$ mapped through $\mathbf Z_\ell\subset E$. Let $M_n(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E V_n)$ with its finite-dimensional product norm topology, and use the induced $G\times H$-action. Form $M=\operatorname{colim}_{n\geq0} M_n$ in the category of internal $A$-modules with this action; this is a sheaf colimit, without completing its sections or imposing a uniform nilpotence bound. Let $D$ be the induced internal endomorphism and let $\tau=1\in H$. Thus $\tau-1=\exp(D)-1$ is an internal endomorphism of $M$, defined at every finite stage by the finite sum above.

Write $\Gamma_H^G:\mathcal A_{G\times H}(A)\to\mathcal A_G(A)$ for the $H$-fixed-submodule functor retaining the $G$-action, with the inflation adjunction of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]. In the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], there is an isomorphism
$$R\Gamma_H^G(M[0])\ \cong\ Q\bigl([\,M\xrightarrow{\ \exp(D)-1\ }M\,]\bigr)\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal A_G(A)),$$
where the displayed complex is in degrees $0,1$ and $Q$ denotes localization of complexes. The isomorphism induces in degree zero the identification of $H$-fixed sections with $\ker(\exp(D)-1)$ given by their common inclusion in $M$. The derived functor is the ordinary right derived functor in the full action category, not a derived functor computed only within the displayed class of modules. The assertion includes $G=1$, zero stages, $D_n=0$, and unbounded dimensions and nilpotence orders. For $F=\Omega$ the noncomplete norm topology and all continuous maps are retained.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model] to $R=A$, $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $u:\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}\to H$, $k\mapsto k$. For every module $N$ with commuting $G,H$ actions this constructs the actual morphism $c_N^G:R\Gamma_H^G(N[0])\to Q[N\xrightarrow{\tau-1}N]$. It belongs to a transformation of triangulated functors on $D^+$, and forgetting $G$ takes it to the scalar-action version $c_N^1$ and reflects its invertibility. It therefore suffices to establish that $c_M^1$ is an isomorphism after forgetting $G$. This use does not assume that dense restriction is an isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; scalar analytic base, nilpotent extension devissage and filtered passage below the polynomial translation acyclicity input.

proof.text: First take the trivial $H$-module $A$. Form the underived scalar bar $U_A^q(S)=C(S\times H^q,F)$ and its canonical augmentation $j_A:QU_A^\bullet\to\mathscr B_A(H)$. For $F=E$, [lem-sfb-normed-scalar-profinite-hom-acyclic] applies to every profinite $P=H^q$ and gives the columnwise resolution quasi-isomorphisms. The bar faces respect them by that node's parameter naturality. The first-quadrant column-comparison theorem makes their total $j_A$ an isomorphism; the source columns are concentrated in resolution degree zero. For $F=\Omega$, use instead [lem-sfb-norm-algcl-bar-augmentation] for this actual total augmentation. The complete-field lemma is not applied to $\Omega$, and no individual internal-Hom acyclicity for $\Omega$ is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; scalar analytic base, nilpotent extension devissage and filtered passage below the polynomial translation acyclicity input.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-procyclic-scalar-cochain-evaluation], the map $\epsilon:U_A^\bullet\to[A\xrightarrow0 A]$ that is the identity in degree zero and evaluates a one-cochain at $1$ in degree one is a quasi-isomorphism of the explicit function-sheaf complexes. The cited statement gives equality of image and kernel sheaves, allowing local primitives after a finite jointly surjective parameter cover; no global sectionwise exactness is required. The formal normalization in [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model] gives $c_A^1\eta^{-1}j_A=Q\epsilon$, where $\eta:R\Gamma_H A\simeq\mathscr B_A(H)$. Since $j_A,\eta,Q\epsilon$ are invertible, so is $c_A^1$. This proves the scalar base case with the specific comparison map, rather than merely its cohomology groups.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; scalar analytic base, nilpotent extension devissage and filtered passage below the polynomial translation acyclicity input.

proof.text: Fix a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $W$ and a nilpotent $D_W$. A choice of basis identifies $C(-,F\otimes_E W)$ with a finite biproduct of $A$ as internal modules. In the case $D_W=0$, $H$ acts trivially, so the same is an equivariant isomorphism. The two functors defining $c^1$ are additive and the transformation is natural by [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model]. On a finite biproduct its components are therefore copies of $c_A^1$. This proves invertibility for every trivial finite-dimensional stage, including $W=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; scalar analytic base, nilpotent extension devissage and filtered passage below the polynomial translation acyclicity input.

proof.text: For a general finite stage put $W_0=\ker D_W$. It is $H$-stable and $H$ acts trivially on it. The quotient $\overline W=W/W_0$ has the induced nilpotent operator and exponential action. Choose an $E$-linear complement to $W_0$ by extending a basis; in finite-dimensional product norm coordinates inclusion and quotient are continuous and the chosen section is continuous. After $F\otimes_E-$ and $C(S,-)$ this gives a split exact sequence on every $S$, hence a short exact sequence of internal $H$-modules $0\to M(W_0)\to M(W)\to M(\overline W)\to0$. The splitting is used only to prove underlying exactness, and is not asserted equivariant. Exponentials commute with the maps because they are finite polynomials in $D_W$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; scalar analytic base, nilpotent extension devissage and filtered passage below the polynomial translation acyclicity input.

proof.text: Induct on $\dim_E W$. The zero-dimensional case was covered in step 4, and $D_W=0$ is also covered there. If $D_W\ne0$, nilpotence gives $\ker D_W\ne0$: for a nonzero vector take its last nonzero iterate under $D_W$. Thus $\dim\overline W<\dim W$; the kernel has trivial action and the quotient satisfies the same finite-stage hypotheses. The short exact sequence of step 5 gives a distinguished triangle by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. The comparison $c^1$ is compatible with that triangle and its boundary by [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model]. Triangle two-out-of-three applied to the kernel and quotient comparisons proves $c^1_{M(W)}$ invertible. In particular it holds for every original $M_n$, with no relation between the different exponents $e_n$ required.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; scalar analytic base, nilpotent extension devissage and filtered passage below the polynomial translation acyclicity input.

proof.text: Now forget $G$ from the original sequence and take its sheaf colimit $M$. [lem-sfb-profinite-invariants-filtered-continuity], applied to $J=H$ and $I=\mathbf N$, identifies $\operatorname{colim}_n H^q(R\Gamma_HM_n)$ with $H^q(R\Gamma_HM)$ by the actual coprojection maps, for every $q\ge0$. Its statement also ensures that the forgotten module is this same sheaf colimit. On the two-term side, exact filtered colimits commute with kernels, images and cokernels, hence with cohomology of $[M_n\xrightarrow{\tau-1}M_n]$. Exactness is the Grothendieck/AB5 property of these action and underlying module categories in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. The target differential is the colimit differential because all transition maps commute with the actions.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; scalar analytic base, nilpotent extension devissage and filtered passage below the polynomial translation acyclicity input.

proof.text: Naturality of $c^1$ for every coprojection gives, for each $q\ge0$, a commutative square whose top arrow is $\operatorname{colim}_n H^q(c_{M_n}^1)$ and whose bottom arrow is $H^q(c_M^1)$; its two vertical arrows are exactly the comparisons of step 7. The top arrow is an isomorphism by step 6, so the bottom arrow is an isomorphism. In negative degrees both sides have zero cohomology, since right derived invariants on a degree-zero module and the two-term complex are bounded below by zero. Thus $c_M^1$ is an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category, in which quasi-isomorphisms are inverted. No infinite nilpotent induction or uniform nilpotence exponent was used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; scalar analytic base, nilpotent extension devissage and filtered passage below the polynomial translation acyclicity input.

proof.text: Restore the $G$-action. By the conservative forgetting and comparison clause of [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model], the image of $c_M^G$ under forgetting $G$ is the isomorphism $c_M^1$ just proved. Hence $c_M^G$ is invertible in $D(\mathcal A_G(A))$. Its target is the required complex: at stage $n$, $\tau$ acts by the given finite exponential $\exp(D_n)$, and compatibility with transition maps identifies its colimit action with $\exp(D)$. Thus $\tau-1=\exp(D)-1$. This proves the derived-object assertion with its commuting residual action.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; scalar analytic base, nilpotent extension devissage and filtered passage below the polynomial translation acyclicity input.

proof.text: The formal comparison has its invariant-inclusion normalization, so its degree-zero map identifies the two subobjects by their inclusions in $M$. One can also check their equality directly without assuming separatedness of the colimit topology: on a finite stage write $\exp(D_n)-1=D_n U(D_n)$ where $U(X)=\sum_{j=1}^{e_n}X^{j-1}/j!$. The endomorphism $U(D_n)$ has the form $1+$ a nilpotent polynomial and is invertible by a finite geometric sum, commuting with $D_n$. Hence its difference kernel is $\ker D_n$, which is fixed by every $\exp(tD_n)$, including continuously varying $t$. A section of the sheaf colimit is locally from a stage; if its difference is zero, refine locally to a later stage where that equation holds. The finite-stage argument then proves it fixed after every base change. Conversely $H$-fixed sections are fixed by $1\in H$. Thus the common inclusion is exactly the required one. All arguments include zero stages and $D_n=0$, and only finite-stage nilpotence was used.
